In 2023, by United Nations estimates, India passed China to become the most populous country in the world, with more than 1.4 billion people, about one in six of humanity. China had held that place for centuries.

The crossing came from two different paths. China's births fell sharply under the one child policy from 1980 and kept falling after it ended, and its population began to shrink in 2022. India's fertility fell more slowly, through schooling, cities and family planning, and reached about two children per woman, the replacement level, only around 2020.

India is also young: its median age is under 30, about ten years below China's. Economists speak of a demographic dividend if those young people find work, and a burden if they do not. The exact count is uncertain, because the census due in 2021 was put off. For earlier turns in the same story see China's population surge and Japan's population peaks; for the state itself, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka.
